summary:
Cluster E supplies the paper's two base-change/obstruction items (8-9). Item 8 is the exact-Kahn-base-change propagation of the canonical resolution: a purely topological cartesianity proposition showing that if the localized inclusion at one Kahn stage factors as (universal covering) followed by (embedding), then forming the full, unselected exact Kahn equalizer at the next stage produces the pullback covering, an embedded second leg, identical kernel pairs, and fiberwise bijections -- so the infinite canonical sheet defect propagates verbatim through every full exact Kahn equalizer on the complementary-cover locus. Item 9 is the whole-tile correspondence no-go: after typing the two systems (the canonical resolved factorization with its annular-tower deck structure G = N x| H, and the actual boundary-extended Kahn--Lyubich universal-cover tile with its two source-locked infinitely-wrapping vertices), a five-clause "whole-tile end-compatible comparison" is defined, and Theorem 5.1 proves that any such comparison forces the deck kernel N to be trivial. Since the ordinary primitive canonical resolution has infinite sheet defect (preserved by item 8's base change), Corollary 5.2 concludes that the canonical infinite resolution is never a whole boundary-extended KL tile, and Corollary 5.3 records the exact optional identification that fails. The cluster also delivers the finite obstruction certificate (no numerics, no local-connectivity input) and the sharply delimited list of interfaces the no-go leaves admissible: proper interior/collar restriction, non-covering immersion or relation-valued comparison, retiming to a trivial-kernel stage (impossible inside the unchanged equalizer tower), and localization revision restoring subgroup reflection.

Crucially, the no-go is an impossibility theorem about a comparison square, not about the KL map: it does not prove the actual KL inclusion immersion injective (an explicit non-covering immersion control blocks that upgrade), does not decide whether the same-seed comparison class is empty or nonempty, and constructs none of the four replacement interfaces. All caveats from the source documents are preserved below and must survive editing.

%% ---------------------------------------------------------------
%% Notation for the base-change / tile-obstruction cluster (items 8-9).
%% amsart-compatible; requires only amsmath, amssymb, amsthm.
%% ---------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection*{Notation and standing conventions}

\begin{itemize}
\item \(\mathbb D=\{z\in\mathbb C:\lvert z\rvert<1\}\) is the unit disk, \(\operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb D)\) its group of conformal automorphisms, and \(d_{\mathcal E}\) the hyperbolic metric of a domain \(\mathcal E\cong\mathbb D\).  \(C\Subset\mathcal E\) means that \(C\) has compact closure in \(\mathcal E\).

\item All spaces are Hausdorff.  For a covering map \(p\colon\widehat X\to X\), \(\operatorname{Deck}(p)\) denotes its deck group.  A covering is \emph{universal} when its total space is simply connected; the deck group of a universal covering acts simply transitively on each fiber.  A nonregular infinite covering may have trivial deck group, so the universal typing is part of the data, never a convenience.

\item For a based covering \(p\colon(\widehat X,\widehat x)\to(X,x)\), its subgroup is \(H=p_*\pi_1(\widehat X,\widehat x)\le\pi_1(X,x)\).  For subgroups \(H\le K\), the \emph{pointed coset set} \(K/H=\{kH:k\in K\}\) is a pointed set with basepoint \(H\); no group structure is asserted unless \(H\trianglelefteq K\).

\item \(a\colon(X_s,x_s)\hookrightarrow(X_t,x_t)\) denotes the based topological embedding underlying the canonical localization, with based connected covers of subgroups \(H_s,H_t\), based lift \(A\), and \(K:=a_*^{-1}(H_t)\le\pi_1(X_s,x_s)\), so that \(H_s\le K\).  The \emph{canonical sheet resolution} is the factorization \(A=e\circ q\) through the resolved pullback component, with \(q\) a covering whose based fiber is the pointed coset set \(K/H_s\) and \(e\) a topological embedding; \([K:H_s]\) is the \emph{sheet defect}.  (These are supplied by the resolution cluster; see Theorem~\ref{thm:canonical-sheet-resolution} and Corollary~\ref{cor:infinite-sheet-defect} there.)

\item For maps \(i\colon X\to Z\) and \(f\colon Y\to Z\), the fiber product is \(X\times_ZY=\{(x,y):i(x)=f(y)\}\); the \emph{kernel pair} of \(g\colon X\to Y\) is \(X\times_YX\).  A commutative square is \emph{cartesian} when it is a pullback square.

\item \(\mathbf U^r\) denotes the \(r\)-th stage of the exact Kahn equalizer tower on the complementary-cover locus, with the two stage maps \(i_r,f_r\colon\mathbf U^{r+1}\to\mathbf U^{r}\) (localized inclusion and dynamics), so that
\(\mathbf U^{r+2}=\{(x,y)\in\mathbf U^{r+1}\times\mathbf U^{r+1}:i_r(x)=f_r(y)\}\) and \(i_{r+1}(x,y)=y\).

\item For a discrete subgroup \(\Gamma\le\operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb D)\), \(\Lambda(\Gamma)\subset\partial\mathbb D\) is its limit set; \(\Gamma\) is \emph{elementary} when \(\Lambda(\Gamma)\) contains at most two points.  A hyperbolic element of \(\operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb D)\) has one repelling and one attracting fixed point on \(\partial\mathbb D\).

\item Overlines denote continuous extensions to conformal ideal closures, e.g.\ \(\overline\Phi\), \(\overline L_{\mathrm{KL}}\).  The ideal closures of the Kahn--Lyubich pseudo-pieces used here are the Hausdorff conformal ideal closures of the source texts; on the resolved side the point-valued ideal boundary is formed after the Fuchsian limit set has been removed (Kahn~I, \texttt{wad.tex}, lines 169--175).

\item \(\widehat A_s,\widehat A_t\) denote the source and target universal-cover tiles of an actual Kahn--Lyubich pseudo-piece (KL~II, \texttt{psiql.tex}, lines 118--123); \(t_s\) is the positive source annular deck generator; \(\omega_-,\omega_+\in\partial\widehat A_s\) are its two fixed prime ends, identified by the source with the named infinitely wrapping \(\lambda/J\) vertices; \(L_{\mathrm{KL}}\colon\widehat A_s\to\widehat A_t\) is one source-indexed actual KL inclusion tile map.

\item \(\mathcal E,\mathcal R,T,q,e,L,N,G,H,h,\zeta_\pm\) always refer to the canonical resolved system and its annular-tower typing, Definition~\ref{def:canonical-resolved-system}.
\end{itemize}

theorems.name: Normal-kernel wrapping incidence (imported lemma)
theorems.label: lem:wrapping
theorems.proof_latex:
\begin{proof}
Let \(\pi\colon G\to\mathbb Z\) be the projection determined by the splitting \eqref{eq:semidirect}, normalized by \(\pi(h)=1\); its kernel is \(N\).  As a deck group acting freely on \(\mathcal E\cong\mathbb D\), \(G\) is discrete and torsion-free.

Suppose first that \(G\) were elementary.  A torsion-free elementary discrete subgroup of \(\operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb D)\) is cyclic; since \(G\) contains the hyperbolic element \(h\), write \(G=\langle g\rangle\) and \(h=g^m\).  Then
\[
1=\pi(h)=m\,\pi(g)
\]
in \(\mathbb Z\), forcing \(m=\pm1\).  Hence \(G=\langle h\rangle=H\) and \(N=\ker\pi=\{1\}\), contrary to hypothesis.  Therefore \(G\) is non-elementary.

The subgroup \(N\) is nontrivial and normal in \(G\).  Its limit set \(\Lambda(N)\) is nonempty, closed, and \(G\)-invariant: normality gives
\[
g\,\Lambda(N)=\Lambda(gNg^{-1})=\Lambda(N)
\qquad\text{for every } g\in G.
\]
If \(\Lambda(N)\) were finite, its one- or two-point set would be preserved by \(G\), making \(G\) elementary.  Thus \(\Lambda(N)\) is infinite.  Choose
\[
\alpha\in\Lambda(N)\setminus\{\zeta_-,\zeta_+\}.
\]
Because \(h\) normalizes \(N\), every \(h^k\alpha\) belongs to \(\Lambda(N)\).  Hyperbolic dynamics of \(h\) on \(\partial\mathbb D\) gives
\[
h^k\alpha\to\zeta_+\quad(k\to+\infty),
\qquad
h^k\alpha\to\zeta_-\quad(k\to-\infty).
\]
Closedness of \(\Lambda(N)\) proves \eqref{eq:wrapping-in-limit-set}.
\end{proof}
theorems.caveats: Imported: this lemma is proved in the companion resolved-intermediate ideal-boundary pass (resolved_intermediate_relative_ideal_boundary.md, its Lemma 8.1) and is restated here in the cluster's notation; if another cluster of the paper also transcribes it, deduplicate at assembly.  The normality \(N\trianglelefteq G\), the split \(G=N\rtimes H\), and non-elementarity are essential: the proof never asserts \(h\in N\) and never writes \(q(hz)=q(z)\); without normality (or an independent proof of the limit-set incidence) a cyclic \(N\) may have two entirely different fixed points and the wrapping conclusion fails.

theorems.name: Base-change propagation through exact equalizers (cartesianity)
theorems.label: prop:base-change
theorems.proof_latex:
\begin{proof}
(1)  The displayed square is a pullback by direct substitution in the definitions: a point of \(X\times_PR\) is a pair \((x,(p,y))\) with \(q(x)=p\) and \(e(p)=f(y)\), which is exactly a pair \((x,y)\) with \(e(q(x))=f(y)\), i.e.\ with \(i(x)=f(y)\); thus \(X\times_PR=X\times_ZY=E\), with \(q'\) corresponding to the second projection.  The pullback of a covering is a covering, so \(q'\) is a covering; it is surjective because for \((p,y)\in R\) any \(x\in q^{-1}(p)\) satisfies \(i(x)=e(q(x))=e(p)=f(y)\), so \((x,y)\in E\) and \(q'(x,y)=(p,y)\).

(2)  If \(e'(p_1,y_1)=e'(p_2,y_2)\), then \(y_1=y_2=y\).  Membership in \(R\) gives
\[
e(p_1)=f(y)=e(p_2),
\]
and injectivity of \(e\) gives \(p_1=p_2\).  On the image \(\{y\in Y:f(y)\in e(P)\}\) the inverse is
\[
y\longmapsto\bigl(e^{-1}(f(y)),\,y\bigr),
\]
which is continuous because \(e\) is an embedding (so \(e^{-1}\) is continuous on \(e(P)\)).  Hence \(e'\) is a topological embedding.

(3)  Formula \eqref{eq:base-change-maps} gives \(e'(q'(x,y))=e'(q(x),y)=y=i'(x,y)\).

(4)  Since \(e'\) is injective, \(i'(u)=i'(v)\iff e'(q'(u))=e'(q'(v))\iff q'(u)=q'(v)\); the kernel pairs coincide.

(5)  Formula \eqref{eq:fiber-bijection} is immediate from the definition of \(q'\).
\end{proof}
theorems.caveats: Purely topological; no complex analysis or dynamics enters.  The total spaces \(E\) and \(R\) need not be connected: the statement is about the full, unselected equalizer, with no component selection.  The proposition asserts nothing about ideal boundaries, prime ends, or filled completions.

theorems.name: Exact propagation through the Kahn equalizer tower
theorems.label: cor:kahn-tower
theorems.statement_latex:
\begin{corollary}[Propagation through the exact Kahn equalizer tower]\label{cor:kahn-tower}
Kahn's recursion on the complementary-cover locus is exactly such a base change:
\[
\mathbf U^{r+2}=\{(x,y)\in\mathbf U^{r+1}\times\mathbf U^{r+1}:i_r(x)=f_r(y)\},
\qquad
i_{r+1}(x,y)=y.
\]
If \(i_r=e_rq_r\) with \(q_r\) a covering onto the resolved intermediate \(P_r\) and \(e_r\) an embedding, then setting
\[
P_{r+1}=P_r\times_{\mathbf U^r}\mathbf U^{r+1},
\qquad
q_{r+1}(x,y)=(q_r(x),y),
\qquad
e_{r+1}(p,y)=y,
\]
one has \(i_{r+1}=e_{r+1}q_{r+1}\), with \(q_{r+1}\) the pullback covering of \(q_r\), \(e_{r+1}\) a topological embedding, the kernel pairs of \(i_{r+1}\) and \(q_{r+1}\) equal, and, for every \((p,y)\in P_{r+1}\),
\[
q_{r+1}^{-1}(p,y)\cong q_r^{-1}(p).
\]
By induction on \(r\), the resolved factorization and its infinite full fibers propagate through every full, unselected exact Kahn equalizer on the complementary-cover locus.
\end{corollary}
theorems.caveats: Faithful scope limits from the source (kl_localization_sheet_resolution_factorization.md, Section 6 end matter and Section 9): the propagation holds only through the full, unselected exact Kahn equalizers on the complementary-cover locus.  It does NOT extend the factorization across a filled or prime-end completion; it does NOT identify one selected connected component with the proof-used direct-decoration O-side; it does NOT prove that all required sheets lie in that component; and it does NOT discharge the same-seed alignment hypothesis by itself.  The separate KAHN_ITERATE_COMPLEMENTARY_COMPONENT_ALIGNMENT theorem proves connected ambient and tilewise interior alignment for one fixed eligible seed but constructs no intermediate ideal boundary or O-side.

theorems.name: Whole-tile correspondence no-go (forced trivial kernel)
theorems.label: thm:whole-tile-no-go
theorems.caveats: This theorem does NOT prove that the actual KL immersion is injective: a noninjective holomorphic immersion need not be a covering onto its image and need not carry a global deck-invariance relation, and can therefore extend continuously to its boundary (explicit control: \(F(z)=\exp(4(z-1))\) on \(\mathbb D\), see the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:admissible}).  The minimal target separation actually used is exactly injectivity of \(B\) on \(L(\mathcal E)\): if \(B\) collapses \(L(\mathcal E)\) to a point there is no contradiction, so clause (3) may not be dropped, and conversely no global target homeomorphism is needed.  The theorem may NOT be applied to a collar merely because the collar lies inside \(\mathcal E\): the deck-limit sequence may leave it.  It is consistent with the trivial-kernel positive control: when \(N=\{1\}\) a one-sheeted factorization can be transported whenever the based map-identification and target embedding are independently supplied.  The universal-cover typing of \(q\) is essential (a nonregular infinite cover can have trivial deck group), as are nonconstancy of \(L\) and the Hausdorff property of the KL ideal closure.  The theorem does not invalidate the relative ideal bordification on \(\partial\mathbb D\setminus\Lambda(N)\): a nontrivial cover can extend at points outside its limit set.  Under final-root enlargement, \(N\), \(\Lambda(N)\), and the selected end correspondence may all change; based-coset bijectivity alone does not transport clauses (2)--(5).

theorems.name: Canonical infinite resolution is not a whole boundary-extended KL tile
theorems.label: cor:canonical-not-whole-tile
theorems.statement_latex:
\begin{corollary}[Canonical infinite resolution is not a whole KL tile]\label{cor:canonical-not-whole-tile}
For the ordinary primitive canonical resolution the sheet defect is infinite:
\[
[K:H_s]=\infty.
\]
Therefore no whole-tile end-compatible comparison identifies its covering/embedding factorization with an actual Kahn--Lyubich tile map.
\end{corollary}
theorems.caveats: Depends on the infinite-sheet-defect corollary of the resolution cluster ([K:H_s]=\infty at every ordinary primitive canonical seed, proved by the winding homomorphism about the excess component); the cross-reference label must be reconciled at assembly.  Transport of this statement to a named KL direct-decoration depth still carries the same-seed alignment qualification recorded in the forced-collision theorem.  The universal-cover typing step is essential and must not be paraphrased away: infinite sheet number alone does not produce a nontrivial group acting transitively on a fiber.

theorems.name: Exact optional input that fails
theorems.label: cor:optional-input-fails
theorems.caveats: This locates the first unsupported operation in the former whole-tile route: the identification of the propagated canonical q/e factorization with a covering/embedding factorization of the complete actual KL tile map.  It does NOT decide, without an independent realization theorem, whether a proposed same-seed subclass is empty, whether the canonical factorization corresponds only to a proper subdomain, or whether the correct comparison changes the localization data.  (Quantifier audit: the theorem proves conditional emptiness of the class defined WITH the five-clause comparison; it proves nothing about emptiness or nonemptiness of the class Canonical-and-KL defined without it.)

theorems.name: Exact obstruction certificate
theorems.label: prop:obstruction-certificate
theorems.caveats: The certificate is a record of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:whole-tile-no-go}, not an additional theorem; it should be presented as the referee-checkable finite witness of the obstruction.  It certifies the failure of the five-clause square only.

theorems.name: Scope of the obstruction: admissible replacement interfaces
theorems.label: prop:admissible
theorems.proof_latex:
\begin{proof}
(1)  The contradiction in Theorem~\ref{thm:whole-tile-no-go} is produced by a deck-limit sequence \(\gamma_nz\to\zeta_+\).  Such sequences need not remain in \(C\), and the restricted map \(\Phi_C\) need not satisfy the \(N\)-invariance \eqref{eq:deck-invariance} used in the proof; the argument therefore does not run on \(C\).  Any collar no-go would have to prove invariance or recurrence of the deck-limit sequence inside that collar separately.

(2)  A relation span supplies neither the single-valued composite square (clause (4)) nor the deck-generator conjugation (clause (2)), so no step of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:whole-tile-no-go} applies to it.  This branch is not vacuous, by the following positive control.  Define
\[
F(z)=\exp\bigl(4(z-1)\bigr),\qquad z\in\mathbb D.
\]
Then \(|F(z)|=\exp(4(\operatorname{Re}z-1))<1\), \(F'(z)=4F(z)\ne0\), and \(F\) extends continuously to \(\overline{\mathbb D}\).  It is noninjective because
\[
F(\pi i/4)=F(-\pi i/4)=-e^{-4}.
\]
It is not a covering onto its image: if it were, the simply connected domain would make it the universal cover, whose deck group acts transitively on every fiber.  A deck transformation \(\delta\) carrying \(\pi i/4\) to \(-\pi i/4\) would satisfy \(\exp(4(\delta(z)-1))=\exp(4(z-1))\), so the continuous function \(4(\delta(z)-z)/(2\pi i)\) would be integer-valued on the connected disk, hence constant; its value at \(\pi i/4\) is \(-1\), so \(\delta(z)=z-\pi i/2\), which is not an automorphism of \(\mathbb D\).  Thus noninjectivity together with continuous boundary extension is compatible exactly when the noninjectivity is not a global covering-deck invariance.

(3)  If \(N=\{1\}\), there is no nontrivial deck element, hence no sequence \eqref{eq:deck-seq}, and the deck-limit obstruction is absent; a one-sheeted factorization can be transported to the actual KL tile whenever the based map-identification and target embedding are independently supplied.  For the preservation claim: any stage reached from the canonical seed by finitely many full exact Kahn equalizer base changes has, by Corollary~\ref{cor:kahn-tower}, fibers in bijection with the seed fiber, which is infinite; hence \(N\) remains infinite at every such stage, and a trivial-kernel stage cannot be reached by retiming inside the unchanged tower.

(4)  If the revised subgroup data satisfies \(a_*^{-1}(H_t)=H_s\), then by the injectivity clause of the canonical sheet-resolution theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:canonical-sheet-resolution}: \(q\) is injective if and only if \(K=H_s\)) the revised resolution is one-sheeted, so \(N=\{1\}\) and Theorem~\ref{thm:whole-tile-no-go} imposes no constraint; conversely, if the reflection equality fails, the revised \(q\) is again a nontrivial covering.  The proviso that the physical embedding lifts between the revised covers is part of the hypothesis and is not established here.
\end{proof}
theorems.caveats: The four branches are NOT proved exhaustive of all possible interfaces (restricted-interface classification, verdict scope).  None of the obligations (1)(a)-(d), the relation bookkeeping in (2), the universal bounded retiming rule in (3), or the dynamical-package/obstacle/access/final-root preservation in (4) is discharged by this proposition; each replacement must prove its own component, access, ideal-boundary, properness, and final-root clauses.  No checked source proves that a localization revision preserving the reflection equality also preserves the required dynamical package.  Item (4)'s equivalence cites the resolution cluster's Theorem (label to reconcile at assembly).

warnings: Never state or imply that the no-go proves the actual KL inclusion immersion injective. The source is explicit that an arbitrary noninjective holomorphic immersion need not be a covering onto its image and can extend continuously to its boundary; the control F(z)=exp(4(z-1)) (transcribed in Proposition prop:admissible) exists precisely to block this upgrade. A referee will attack any stronger phrasing.

Quantifier discipline (source Section 8.12): the theorem proves emptiness only of the class whose definition INCLUDES the five-clause whole-tile end-compatible comparison. It does not prove the independently defined same-seed Canonical-and-KL class empty or nonempty; either inference would need an independent realization theorem.

Clause (5) of the comparison definition requires the biholomorphic based-cover typing of clause (1); algebraic generator conjugacy by an arbitrary interior homeomorphism is insufficient (strip-shear control u(x,y)=(x-1/y,y) in Remark rem:clause5). Do not simplify the definition by deleting clause (5) or by weakening clause (1) to a homeomorphism.

Target separation may not be weakened away: if B collapses L(E) to one point, equation (constant-value) yields no contradiction. The proof uses exactly injectivity of B on L(E) and nothing more; conversely no global target homeomorphism is required.
The no-go must not be applied to collar or interior restrictions: the deck-limit sequence may leave the retained set. Any collar-level no-go requires a separate invariance or recurrence proof.

Universal-cover typing of q is essential: a nonregular infinite cover can have trivial deck group, so 'infinite sheet number' alone does not supply the acting group N used in the proof. Corollary cor:canonical-not-whole-tile's step from infinite fiber to N infinite uses simple transitivity of Deck on fibers of a universal covering.

The wrapping lemma (lem:wrapping) needs normality N normal in G, the split G = N x| H, and non-elementarity; the proof never writes q(hz)=q(z) and h is not asserted to lie in N. It is proved in resolved_intermediate_relative_ideal_boundary.md (its Lemma 8.1) and restated here; deduplicate with the cluster covering that document.
Nonconstancy of L and the Hausdorff property of the KL conformal ideal closure are both load-bearing hypotheses (source Section 8.11) and may not be deleted in editing.

Proposition prop:base-change / Corollary cor:kahn-tower propagate the factorization ONLY through full, unselected exact Kahn equalizers on the complementary-cover locus. They do not cross filled or prime-end completions, do not select components, do not identify the direct-decoration O-side, do not prove all required sheets lie in one component, and do not discharge same-seed alignment; the alignment theorem is separate and constructs no intermediate ideal boundary.

Final-root enlargement may change N, its limit set, and the selected end correspondence; based-coset bijectivity alone does not transport clauses (2)-(5). Any enlargement theorem must give a Cartesian map square and an equivariant map of relative boundary components while preserving every excluded limit-set defect.

The no-go does not invalidate the relative ideal bordification on the domain of discontinuity (boundary minus Lambda(N)): a nontrivial cover can extend at points outside its limit set (strip-model control).

Cross-cluster references: Theorem thm:canonical-sheet-resolution (canonical sheet resolution, its clause 'q injective iff K = H_s') and Corollary cor:infinite-sheet-defect ([K:H_s] = infinity via the winding homomorphism) are cited by label and must be supplied by the cluster covering kl_localization_sheet_resolution_factorization.md; reconcile labels at assembly.

Do not import the 'full pseudo-piece gluing theorem' of kl_relative_overlap_cartesianity.md in universal full-canonical form anywhere in the paper: its tile-injectivity antecedent is FALSE for the full canonical primitive localization (the forced-collision class gives a non-base element of a_*^{-1}(H_t)/H_s and actual noninjectivity of the full bold base-annulus map, every induced full tile map, and the glued pseudo-piece map). It survives only as a conditional theorem for separately realized collision-free maps or retained collars.

Transport of Corollary cor:canonical-not-whole-tile to a named KL direct-decoration depth carries the same-seed alignment qualification recorded in the forced-collision theorem; state it wherever depth-specific claims are made.

Nothing in this cluster promotes any global obligation: DIRECT_DECORATION_OUTER_CAP_FOOTPRINT, pseudo-piece path-lift exhaustion, all Virtual-Wave certificates, VAAPC-I, UPTCR, and MLC remain open, and the four admissible replacement interfaces are nominated, not constructed.
